<!-- chapter: guides/first-short.md -->
# Your First 60-Second Short: A 7-Day Plan

One finished minute. That's the goal — not a masterpiece, a *finished* film. Sixty seconds forces every discipline in this guide into one small, shippable object: story, prompting, generation, selects, sound, grade, export. Follow the days in order. Each day links the exact chapters, skills, and tools to use, and ends with a checkpoint: don't move on until it passes.

**Rules for the week:** one character, one location, no dialogue longer than two short lines (write around talking — visual storytelling wins at this length). Budget: one cheap draft model for days 2–3, your best model only for final hero shots. Track spend in the budget calculator as you go.

## Day 1 — Concept lock

**Do:** write one logline (protagonist + want + obstacle, one sentence), then a 6-beat outline: setup, turn 1, turn 2, midpoint image, turn 3, button. Pick your one location and describe it in three sensory sentences — this description becomes your style anchor for the whole week.

**Use:** `craft/story-structure.md` (beats), the prompt workshop's logline template (`workshop.html`).

**Checkpoint:** you can pitch the film in 20 seconds without notes. If you can't, the concept isn't locked — simplify until you can.

## Day 2 — Prompt workshop session

**Do:** generate your hero frame first — the single perfect still of your character in your location. Lock identity before anything moves (this is the take-casting decision). Then write one full prompt per shot (8–12 shots for 60 seconds) using the nine-layer anatomy: subject, action with tactics, setting, light, camera, lens behavior, texture, negative constraints, audio note.

**Use:** `higgsfield/prompt-engineering.md`, `workshop.html` (save your prompts — you'll iterate on them), the `audio-lip-sync-route` skill if you have any dialogue at all.

**Checkpoint:** every prompt has an exclusion block ("no morphing faces, no extra fingers, no text"). No exclusions, no generation.

## Day 3 — Generation batches

**Do:** generate in cheap drafts first. Batch each shot 3–5 takes on your draft model, then pick selects — don't direct yet, just collect. Price the day before you start (credit math × takes) and hold a credit floor: if spend passes plan by ~15%, stop and re-plan.

**Use:** `platforms/when-to-use-what.md` (or the quiz: `quiz.html`), `economics/credit-math.md`, `budget.html`.

**Checkpoint:** you have selects for every shot — imperfect, but every story beat exists on screen. Gaps get re-prompted tomorrow, not tonight.

## Day 4 — Selects & assembly

**Do:** cut the radio edit — selects in story order, no polish. This is where the film either works or doesn't, and it's cheaper to discover now. If a character drifts between shots, fix it with the consistency tools (reference frames, re-generated hero angles) rather than accepting it. Once a take is approved, lock it: re-render the camera around the performance, never the performance around the camera.

**Use:** `craft/editing-pipeline.md`, `craft/character-consistency.md`, `craft/directing-performance.md` (the Scene Lock rule).

**Checkpoint:** the cut plays start to finish and the story reads with the sound off. If it doesn't read silent, no amount of sound will save it.

## Day 5 — Performance fixes

**Do:** watch like a director, not a generator. For each shot that feels dead: first try restraint (strip adjectives, give the eyes a job, widen the frame), then try one targeted re-generation, then — if it still fails — cut around it. Read the failure gallery before you re-roll anything: most "bad generations" are direction problems with known fixes.

**Use:** `craft/directing-performance.md`, `craft/failure-gallery.md`, the shot teardown viewer (`teardown.html`) for reference.

**Checkpoint:** no shot embarrasses you. "Good enough" is a finishable standard; "perfect" is how films die at 80%.

## Day 6 — Sound

**Do:** build the full audio pass in order: ambient bed under every scene, foley on movement, voice/dialogue on its own track (Road A or B — chosen per scene, never mixed mid-scene), score built cue-by-cue to the locked cut, then the mix (dialogue on top, headroom left, phone-speaker test). Save generation receipts for every AI voice and music cue.

**Use:** `craft/sound-music-audio.md`, the `audio-sfx-bed`, `audio-direct-voiceover`, and `audio-final-mix` skills, the audio checklist at the end of the chapter.

**Checkpoint:** mute the music — the film still plays. Unmute — nothing fights the dialogue.

## Day 7 — Grade, mix QC, export

**Do:** apply one consistent grade across all shots (a single LUT or node tree, adjusted per shot — never a different look per shot). Run the mix QC: three listening environments, loudness sane, no clipping. Export to your delivery spec, watch the export all the way through on a different screen than you edited on, then ship it — upload, submit, or screen it for one human.

**Use:** `craft/color-grading.md`, `distribution/release-paths.md` (delivery specs), `legal/rights-and-disclosure.md` (before anything public — disclosure and rights, not legal advice).

**Checkpoint:** a stranger can watch it end-to-end without you explaining anything. That's a finished film. Everything after this is your second one.

## After the week

Do a 20-minute post-mortem while it's fresh: what broke, what the fix was, what you'd prompt differently. Write it down — that's the seed of your personal playbook, and it's worth more than any tutorial. Then start film two: the same 7 days, twice as fast.

# Interactive Tools (site/)

- `site/teardown.html` — shot-by-shot teardown viewer: Passport Rush, ONEIRIC, the Grok Odyssey $100K winner, Google DeepMind's Dear Upstairs Neighbors, Fountain 0's Dreams of Violets (75-min Tribeca 2026 AI feature, $2K budget), Nikolay Shestak's The First Honest Day ($450K Astana 2026 Grand Prix winner; tools undisclosed — the teardown is honest about the gap), and StoReel's The $150 Microdrama ('Off Campus' experiment: four AI episodes in four days, documented clip by clip) broken into shots (setup / what works / what breaks / craft lesson, labeled prompt reconstructions where the stack is documented); data in `api/v1/teardowns.json`
- `site/manifesto.html` — positioning: a living free reference, not a course; everything sourced; what it won't do
- `site/field-guides/` — printable one-pagers generated from the guide's own data: model quick-reference (from `models.json`), prompt anatomy cheat sheet, consistency & dead-eyes checklist
- `site/api.html` — human-readable API docs + a Try-the-API console (endpoint picker, fetch, pretty-printed JSON), and pointers to `AGENT.md`
- `site/skills.html` — browsable skills library with live filter
- `site/budget.html` — interactive credit-budget calculator
- `site/optimizer.html` — budget optimizer: runtime + dialogue share + quality bar → optimal model mix per bucket from `models.json`, with 5×/20× cost envelopes
- `site/shots.html` — shot-list builder: per-shot type/model/seconds/takes → live cost table from `models.json`, totals with 5×/20× envelopes, localStorage lists, JSON export/import, one-click handoff to the optimizer
- `site/doctor.html` — failure doctor: pick the symptom (face morph, dead eyes, plasticky skin…) → craft diagnosis + fix + deep link into the workshop's repair templates; 12 diagnoses in `api/v1/diagnoses.json` (+ schema)
- `site/linter.html` — prompt linter: paste any prompt → structural analysis against the ten-layer anatomy (layers present/missing, vague words flagged, concrete fix per gap); heuristic, honest about it; one-click handoffs to the workshop and anatomy builder (`assets/js/linter.js`)
- `site/models/` — model deep dives: one page per model (29) + index, generated from `api/v1/models.json` at build time — spec record, worked cost math (USD at $0.0392/credit), use-when/avoid-when from the model's own fields, prompt tips linking the guide's chapters
- `site/anatomy.html` — anatomy of a prompt: interactive nine-layer annotated example + build-your-own mode
- `site/workshop.html` — interactive prompt workshop (template × model × track, save/rate, optional style-bible prepend from `site/style-bible.html`)
- `site/style-bible.html` — style-bible builder: describe character/world once → reusable STYLE LOCK block; named bibles in localStorage (`afg-style-bibles`), copy/save/export/import, workshop integration
- `site/episode-planner.html` — episode planner: lock a mini-drama series (title, logline, hashtag, cast with voice IDs + anchors), plan episode blocks (one emotion, 3–5 beats, turn, cliffhanger), arc tracker with lessons; saved blocks feed one-click 'Send series to Studio' — the planner stages title/logline/cast anchors/every block's format, runtime, and beats into the Studio's series mode; localStorage (`afg-episode-series`)
- `site/hook-generator.html` — hook-title generator: `[Episode N] + [one-line emotional stake] + [CTA]` → 5 worked caption variants, each with a why-this-hooks note
- `site/studio.html` — Studio 2.0 — AI-film studio simulator: a standalone film (title, logline, genre/mood, runtime, draft/festival tier) or a serialized series (3–10 episodes, one of the 5 proven serialized format presets: mini-drama / POV micro-series / day-in-the-life / revenge arc / interactive — each pre-filling runtime band, beat structure, hook style, the dialogue-budget rule) in → deterministic production packet — shot list with per-shot prompts built from the 47-template library, per-shot model picks from `models.json` with cost math, budget table with 5×/20× envelopes, shooting schedule, series bible with locked prompt DNA + locked-anchor asset reuse, self-contained HTML/Markdown packet export (download, print), localStorage plans with names, duplicate, delete, continue-planning; one-click 'Send to Studio' bridge from the episode planner
- `site/quiz.html` — model-picker quiz: 5 questions → ranked top-3 from `models.json` with cost math, one-click handoff to the workshop
- `site/compare.html` — model compare: 2–3 models side by side (cost, best use, strengths, weaknesses, native audio, status/last-verified) from `models.json`, shareable via URL params; discontinued excluded
- `site/gallery.html` — prompt gallery: your workshop-saved prompts (localStorage) browsable, filterable by track/model, sortable by rating, open-in-workshop deep links, JSON export/import
- `site/model-watch.html` — model freshness page: all 29 models with last-verified dates, status (active/reported/announced/discontinued), what changed, sources; "verify live before spending" banner; generated from `models.json` at build time
- `site/checks/` — knowledge checks: 6 scenario-based quizzes (5 questions each) for prompt engineering, directing performance, character consistency, long-form pipelines, sound/music/audio, rights & disclosure; answers explain why, progress in localStorage (`assets/js/checks.js`, data in `scripts/checks.json`)
- `site/changelog.html` — dated changelog rebuilt from git history
- `site/skill-spec.html` — the skill frontmatter+sections format as a spec
- `site/search-index.json` — client-side search index (Ctrl+K palette)
